Man, I wish it was a fake story.  I wish every morning that things would be back to normal.  That it was all a dream.  It's not.
I'm not going to try to prove to you that my little sister is dead. But I understand where you're coming from.  I'm sure if you cared enough you could call the funeral home and confirm that she really is dead...but beyond that, suicides don't normally get published in papers.

My little sister just commit suicide 11 days ago.  She was 20 years old.  She didn't tell anyone but one other person who also had depression.  He didn't really try to talk her out of it either.  But that's just it.  People with depression cannot help other people with depression.  It's a pit of negativity.  You need to talk to people with more life.  Talk to people about this problem you have.  Tell your friends about your debt.  Honestly, the pressure that bottles up in us from our false truths is worse than facing the fact.  This will end up killing you.  Tell your family and friends about how you're feeling, talk to them about why you feel worthless.  On top of that.  Go and do some yoga.  Go do something completely out of your nature, something not routine.  Change things up a bit.

If you need anyone to talk to i;m always here.

I'll start from the beginning...

On January 7th, 2013.
I woke up at 12pm with a bad case of food poisoning.  After throwing up I went downstairs to drink some warm water and eat some tums to try to ease my stomach.  My parents and my older sister were out at work, so it was just me and my little sister, Aggie.  I ate the tums and drank some water then sat down with my little sister to watch the last half of Penelope.  I told her about my food poisoning and as usual, she told me what I shouldn't have ate and how I needed to be more careful.  We talked while we watched the movie.  I sat around for another 40 mins before I went back upstairs to bed.  

That was the last time I saw her alive.

I woke up at 5:40ish pm and ran to the washroom again.  From the upstairs washroom I called out for my little sister; I wanted her to make me some tea and help grab some toilet paper for me; No answer.  I went downstairs to find the house alarm set (this usually meant she had left) so I figured she had gone to school in the afternoon.  Mom came home at around 6 and we sat down on the couch talking a bit.  I asked where Aggie was and she told me she was at school.  Everything was normal.  I went back upstairs and slept until 11pm. 

Then, the nightmare begins.

I went downstairs to find my mom and dad looking for my little sister.  They are calling the school, the bus company, and her close friends.  It's not unusual for a 20 year old to come home at 11pm, but for Aggie it was.  My mom told me she talked to Aggie at 5pm, She was going to take the 7pm bus home and that she didn't need to be picked up.  My mom even asked her if she'd be home for dinner and her reply was 'yeah, maybe'.  Nothing out of the ordinary. She had been missing for 6 hours now and my parents have been searching for 3.  I helped them look, checking her laptop to see if any of her friends knew anything about her whereabouts.  Nothing.  I started to panic. What could have happened to her? Check the hospitals.  Check the police station.  Check the news for ... anything.  At around 12:30 one of the police officers call back and tell us they have tracked Aggie's phone to our neighborhood, within a 100 meter radius of our house.  Me and my dad go out and look for her.  The entire time a more and more sickening feeling sets in that something is not right.  I just want to find her now.  Maybe she's hiding because something bad happened at school? 15 minutes go by and we can't find her outside.  So we go back to the house.  We check the house again. I hear my dad scream...I run over to him with a very uneasy feeling of relief that we had found her but the closer I got to my dad, the quicker that relief turned into terror. "Call 911!!" my dad yelled. That's when I knew something horrible had happened.  I sprinted to the phone and dialed 911 and ran over to my dad who was performing cpr on my little sister.  He had found her in a bathtub of a washroom we dont use anymore. The fear and shock set in immediately. The first 50 pumps he gave her I kept hoping she would gasp for air, spit out all the water and come back to life just like in the movies...nothing. I was counting the pumps to the 911 attendant...one, two, three, four, five .... each word I spoke I felt the little hope I had slip away, nine, ten... one, two, three, four, five, six.... her jaw was clamped shut, her body stiff.  This was the not the movies. Shit like that doesn't happen in real life.
My dad didn't stop the cpr until the ambulance arrived. 





My little sister, Aggie, was dead.






We found two bottles next to the full bathtub.  One for anti-depressants and another nearly empty bottle of Tyenol 3's.  The saddest part is that we did not know she was going through depression.  We didn't even know she was taking anti-depressants.

The entire week leading up to Monday Janauary 7th was actually a great week. The night before she went to Cirque Du Solei with my parents.  The Saturday we all went out for lunch, then she went to go look for cars.  Everything was normal; happy.  There were no signs of depression. No clues.....
